raw_response:
I am a small farmer with only 7 mu and two people in the house, so I will keep the land use simple and put most of my effort into the crops that bring cash and that I already know well. Because my land has well irrigation, I will rely on vegetables more than dryland grain, but I still want some maize for stability. Since my usual system is chili-cabbage, I will keep that as the main rotation on the same 4 mu: chili first, then cabbage after it. That lets me use the land twice in one year and spread my income across seasons. I will put 2 mu into maize because it is steady and less risky, and 1 mu into spinach because it grows fast, needs little land, and gives me quick turnover. I have farmed a long time and my education is limited, so I will not make the plan complicated. I will use hybrid seed for chili, cabbage, and maize to keep yields more reliable, use improved seed for spinach, irrigate according to each crop’s need, and use moderate fertilizer instead of chasing very high input. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor on my small farm and fits the way I manage land now.
